scope: Boulding review that classifies dysfunctional breathing, with hyperventilation syndrome as the first subtype.

keyRecommendations.text: Hyperventilation syndrome is associated with symptoms related to respiratory alkalosis and symptoms independent of hypocapnia.
Other proposed subtypes are periodic deep sighing, thoracic-dominant breathing, forced abdominal expiration, and thoraco-abdominal asynchrony.

clinicalBottomLine: Hyperventilation syndrome is one pattern of dysfunctional breathing, with symptoms both from alkalosis and independent of a low carbon dioxide. It is not the only pattern.
notableCaveats: The Nijmegen questionnaire is named in the search strategy, not validated as a cutoff in the sentences used.

source.title: Dysfunctional breathing: a review of the literature and proposal for classification.
